en.summary: AWS is growing much faster than retail and contributes most operating profit despite a minority of revenue. Underlying operating performance improved, while a prior-year investment gain complicates GAAP earnings comparisons. The main constraint is cash: infrastructure spending exceeds operating cash generation, so cloud growth and returns after investment need separate assessment.
findings: Revenue was $201.944B, changing 12.086% YoY. GAAP diluted EPS was $1.89 versus $1.95 a year ago. These are realized standalone results for 2026-07-01–2026-09-30; changes in the business mix and special items need to be evaluated alongside the consolidated comparison.

GAAP operating income was $28.076B. Dividing it by revenue gives an operating margin of about 13.903%, versus 9.67% a year ago. The financial table separately retains GAAP gross margin of 53.169%. Gross and operating margins measure different expense levels; neither measures cash left after capital investment or the return earned on the installed asset base.

Quarterly operating cash flow was $42.422B versus $35.525B a year ago. Equipment purchases of $77.259B, offset by $1.381B of sales and incentives, leave negative $33.456B of quarterly free cash flow. The headline negative $42.4B covers twelve months. Stronger operating receipts therefore coexist with a larger funding requirement after infrastructure investment.

AWS generated $45.984B of revenue and $17.773B of operating income: approximately 22.8% of consolidated sales but 63.3% of operating profit. This makes cloud profitability disproportionately important to the group. AWS margin is about 38.7%, compared with 7.7% in North America and 3.7% internationally, using the reported segment figures.

GAAP EPS fell from $1.95 to $1.89 even as operating income rose from $17.422B to $28.076B. The year-ago quarter included a $9.5B pretax Anthropic investment gain. A weaker EPS comparison therefore does not imply that the retail/cloud operating profit pool contracted; investment marks and taxes must be evaluated separately.

Prime Day moved largely into Q2 in 2026, making the retail growth comparison uneven. Management guides Q4 revenue to $240B–$247B and operating income to $28.5B–$33.5B, and expects roughly $220B of 2026 cash capital expenditure. These are management expectations. The key test is whether new cloud capacity translates into cash returns as the investment bill rises.

segments.name: AWS
segments.text: Revenue was $45.984B and operating income $17.773B. The release reports approximately 39.3% revenue growth. Capacity utilization, depreciation and customer demand determine whether the current high operating margin can persist as infrastructure expands.

segments.name: North America
segments.text: Revenue was $112.852B and operating income $8.723B. This is the largest sales base, with a substantially lower margin than AWS. Interpret YoY growth alongside the Prime Day shift and fulfillment costs rather than using cloud growth as a proxy for retail demand.

segments.name: International
segments.text: Revenue was $43.108B and operating income $1.580B. Reported growth also reflects currency effects. The lower segment margin means logistics, mix and local pricing changes can materially affect profit even when the revenue change appears modest.

limitations: Analysis uses the listed official filings, releases and financial attachments; official call text has not been fully reviewed.
Product/geographic categories, reportable segments and adjusted measures retain their disclosed perimeters and must not be double-counted or substituted for consolidated GAAP results.
Cash flows are standalone; cumulative disclosures are differenced across adjacent periods. Issuer adjustments, leases and incentives are identified in metric definitions.
No pre-release consensus snapshot was preserved. Management guidance and analytical inferences are distinct from realized results.
